summary: Edge proxy defers flush during repeated small client-chunks and rotated metadata; long streaming completions drop with 499/504
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (AcmeAI, dedicated) reports intermittent stream terminations during long completions. Sessions frequently end with client-side 499 or server-side 504/502 after ~65–120s. This started after the customer rolled a telemetry agent that attaches rotating X-Baggage headers every 10s and issues repeated small chunked POST uploads from their SDK.

Impact:
- Customer sees ~8–12% of long streaming responses fail after ~1–2 minutes.
- Affects production inference for mid-long completions (context lengths >2k).
- User-facing: truncated outputs, retries, and higher token cost.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted endpoint: prod us-east-1, api-gateway -> ALB -> edge-proxy -> serving pool.
- Customer using dedicated capacity pool behind private routing.
- Observed on models: open/ggml-transformer-xl-13b and redwood/llm-internal-compat.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a streaming generate request with a long prompt (approx 2k tokens context).
2) From the client, send the request body in many small chunked writes (client flush every 20–60ms).
3) Every 8–12s the client rotates a large instrumentation header (X-Inst-Baggage ~1.2kB each, cumulative on path due to proxy sticky connection).
4) Wait for streaming completion; intermittently fail between 65–120s with client 499 or server 504.

Observed behaviour / logs (excerpts):
- Edge proxy logs (us-east-edge-22) show repeated Nagle/coalescing behavior and large header frame growth; many connections show "deferred_flush=true" and "idle_write_timeout=65s" annotations.
- ALB access logs: several requests show status_code=504, target_status_code=-1, elapsed_time ~72.45s.
- Customer SDK trace: socket hangup after long silence then immediate reconnect.
- Serving runtime shows no obvious backend OOM; KV-cache warmup completed for affected sessions.

Initial hypothesis:
- The edge proxy (sidecar) is coalescing small client writes into larger buffers and deferring flushes to optimize TCP throughput. When header baggage rotates, the proxy's per-connection header table grows or triggers additional internal buffering which increases time-to-first-byte (TTFB) on warm streams. This interacts with ALB/edge idle-send timeouts and results in mid-stream resets once an idle threshold is hit.
- Alternatively, ALB/NGINX connection-level write stalls due to header/table growth (HTTP/2 HPACK pressure) cause the upstream to consider the connection idle and close it.

Investigation performed so far:
- Reproduced a failure in staging using a synthetic client that mimics small-chunk writes + header rotation; saw similar 504 after ~68s.
- Capture of tcpdump and http2 frames at edge-proxy showed long periods of no outgoing bytes from proxy toward ALB despite incoming client chunks being accepted.
- Increased ALB timeouts in a test harness prevented the 504, confirming timeout sensitivity.
- Temporary mitigation via customer SDK: batching client writes into larger chunks eliminated the failure in repro.

Workarounds suggested to customer:
- Short-term: batch client-side flushes to reduce coalescing artifacts (send at least 2–4KB per write).
- Reduce frequency/size of rotating instrumentation headers; send them as a single stable header if possible.
- If on dedicated, request routing to a different edge pool (we rotated the pool for one session and saw improvement).

Next steps / action items:
- SRE to review edge-proxy flush heuristics and evaluate disabling deferred flush for streaming endpoints. (Assignee: Jared Collins)
- Infra to add a short-lived ALB timeout increase test across a sample of affected customers and monitor for regressions. (Assignee: Ops)
comments: 2026-03-12 Maya Singh: Opened with customer logs attached. Customer reports spike starting 2026-03-09 after deploy of instrumentation agent.

2026-03-12 Jared Collins: Reproduced locally in staging using synthetic client. Observed idle stalls between proxy->alb even though client is streaming. Hypothesis: proxy deferred flush + header growth triggers ALB idle timeout.
2026-03-13 Support (Maya): Applied temporary routing to alternate edge pool for customer. They reported immediate reduction in failures from ~10% to ~1% for an hour.

2026-03-13 SRE (Linh Tran): Collected tcpdump and http2 frame captures; pushing captures to /mnt/ci/artifacts/2026-03-13-edge-buf.tgz and linked in ticket. Noted multiple "PADDING" frames and HPACK table churn.

2026-03-14 Jared Collins: Drafting change to edge-proxy config to remove deferred flush behavior for endpoints flagged as streaming. Will run A/B test on canary nodes. PR: github.com/redwood/release/pull/4387
2026-03-14 Customer (AcmeAI - Todd Rivera): We've applied client batching and reduced header churn; will monitor for 48 hours and report back. Thank you for the quick rotation to alternate pool.
investigation_notes: Repro in staging confirms timing window ~65–75s before ALB emits 504 when proxy defers writes.
HPACK table growth and repeated header rotations increase internal proxy memory accounting and appear to delay actual wire writes to ALB.
No evidence of backend model OOM or serving-runtime CPU starvation during repro.
Increasing ALB idle timeout alleviates but does not address root cause; will need proxy change to guarantee streaming liveness.
SRE to coordinate with infra/network to test edge-proxy config toggle on canary set first.
resolution_notes: In progress: temporary mitigation is client batching and header stabilization. Pending edge-proxy config change and canary rollout. Follow-up: add streaming endpoint tag to bypass deferred flush optimization; monitor for throughput regressions post-rollout.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-Infra: implement edge-proxy toggle to disable deferred flush for streaming endpoints (owner: Jared Collins)
SRE: run 48h canary with 5% of nodes toggled, measure TTFB and overall throughput (owner: Linh Tran)
DX: update SDK guidance about batching and header size for streaming clients (owner: Priya Menon)
